messages:
Sam Lee: Heads up — noticed a weird flicker in the latency dashboard for /v1/generate after yesterday's quota-enforcement rollout. p95 dropped ~20ms but p99 jumped ~180ms, spike concentrated on a couple endpoints.
Anya Patel: hmm, interesting. Is this across all regions or a single cluster? any correlation with quota_rejects or retries?
Sam Lee: single cluster (us-west-2). Not seeing many quota_rejects, but there was an increase in upstream 429->retry flow around the same time. Dashboard: p95 120ms -> 100ms, p99 600ms -> 780ms.
Mike O'Connor: could be retry amplification: a small subset of long tails getting retried and inflating the p99 sample. Do we have request-level route_id breakdown?
Sam Lee: yes — endpoint breakdown shows /v1/generate/streaming (10% of traffic) is responsible for most of the p99 change.
Jess Ramos: can you paste the query you used to generate the percentiles? want to check aggregation vs sampling.
Sam Lee: query I ran in Observability: ```SELECT quantileExact(0.95)(lat_ms) AS p95, quantileExact(0.99)(lat_ms) AS p99 FROM latency WHERE route='/v1/generate/streaming' AND ts > now() - 1h```
Chen Wu: quantileExact is fine, but dashboard uses tdigest rollups for longer windows. Are we comparing direct raw vs rollup numbers? tdigest compression can shift p99 if samples are small.
Anya Patel: good call. Also check whether we include 'retry' tag in the aggregation. If retries are instrumented as separate attempts with the same trace id, they may skew tail.
Sam Lee: digging — our service emits attempt_lat_ms for each retry attempt; the dashboard is currently aggregating attempt_lat_ms without filtering attempts where attempt_index>0. So retries are included.
Mike O'Connor: that sounds like the smoking gun. Inclusion of retry attempts will both lower p95 (more short cached successes) and raise p99 (rare long retries). We should compare by attempt_index==0.
Jess Ramos: quick test: run the same query but WHERE attempt_index=0 and compare. If that correlates, we can either change dashboard to show "first attempt" pctl or annotate with "attempts included".
Sam Lee: ran it: p95=103ms, p99=610ms when attempt_index=0. With attempts included p95=100ms, p99=780ms. So attempts explain most of the delta.
Chen Wu: nice. For rollout UX: we should add a badge in the latency dashboard that indicates whether samples include retries and which metric is shown (attempt vs end-to-end). Low-lift: prefix route label with (attempts-include) or (first-attempt).
Anya Patel: agree. Also add a small note on the rollout checklist: when introducing quota/reject changes, note to check attempt attribution and dashboard sample sources.
Mike O'Connor: also consider a telemetry metric: retry_ratio_by_route and a derived p99_first_attempt vs p99_all_attempts diff alert. If diff > X ms, page on-call.
Jess Ramos: sounds good. I'll open a small ticket to update the dashboard annotations + add a query toggle. Also add a lint rule in telemetry docs to call out 'attempt' vs 'end-to-end' semantics.
Sam Lee: thanks all. I'll add a grafana panel that shows the two p99 lines (attempts vs first) for the last 24h so we can watch canary windows in future rollouts.
deploy-bot: canary: quota-enforcement-v2 rolled to us-west-2 at 2026-03-20T22:10:05Z :white_check_mark:
Chen Wu: one more thing — check client-side SDK retries too. If client retries are happening, they might produce distributed retry attempts that our server attempts don't attribute cleanly.
Sam Lee: noted. I'll look at SDK logs and set a short-lived alert to detect p99 divergence during the next 6h.
Jess Ramos: thanks Sam, filing follow-ups: DOCS-449 (telemetry semantics), DASH-872 (dashboard annotation), ALERT-211 (p99 divergence alert).
Sam Lee: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
